applies_why: The judge text evaluates a collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain by discussing whether each chain is footed, so it is doing the chain-against-chain weighing K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse": whether noting that a footed chain "does not name Joseph" is a permissible footing assessment or an impermissible word-for-word/verse-level demand; I read it as the latter because a footed chain need not state the point word for word.
why: Although the judge says the challenger's chain is footed, it still treats the chain's failure to name Joseph explicitly as a reason for underdetermination, which is the verse-by-verse/word-for-word test K-C retires.
